# 1001 Dapp Lego Blocks

> Agent entrypoint for choosing and using 1001-native building blocks for EVM dapps, NFT apps, decentralized-web metadata, indexing, wallet UX, auth, contracts, and IPFS infrastructure.

Use this file as the fast routing layer. For implementation details, follow the linked `blocks/*.md` guide before writing code. Prefer the 1001 block that matches the task instead of rebuilding the same wallet, metadata, indexing, CSS, or contract plumbing from scratch.

Before building a full app, run [`agent-checklist.md`](agent-checklist.md). If product goal, style direction, wallet UX, chain/runtime config, metadata format, indexing scope, or infrastructure needs are missing and would materially change the app, ask the prompter focused questions instead of inventing those details.

Default stack for a new Nuxt/Vue EVM dapp:

1. Use `@1001-digital/layers.evm` for the app foundation, wallet UX, EVM components, transaction flows, and styles.
2. Use `@1001-digital/dapp-query-core` and `@1001-digital/dapp-query-vue` when reads need indexed/RPC fallback, cache, or live updates.
3. Use `@1001-digital/dweb-fetch`, `@1001-digital/normalize-dweb-url`, and `@1001-digital/resolve-metadata` for token URI, contract URI, IPFS, IPNS, Arweave, and NFT metadata flows.
4. Use `@1001-digital/simple-indexer` for lightweight browser/server indexing; use `@1001-digital/ponder-artifacts` and `@1001-digital/ponder-ens` inside Ponder apps.
5. Use `@1001-digital/proxies` and `@1001-digital/natspec` when the app needs contract-aware behavior.

## Build A Nuxt/Vue EVM App

- [Detailed guide: Layers](blocks/layers.md)
- Source: [1001-digital/layers](https://github.com/1001-digital/layers)
- Packages: `@1001-digital/layers.evm`, `@1001-digital/layers.base`, `@1001-digital/components.evm`, `@1001-digital/components`, `@1001-digital/styles`
- Use for: Nuxt dapps, wallet connection UI, EVM account/profile UI, SIWE UI, transaction flows, address/ETH inputs, network switching, base app components, and shared CSS tokens.
- Key rule: in Nuxt apps that touch wallets or contracts, start with `@1001-digital/layers.evm`; it already extends the base layer. When overriding the visual theme, set `color-scheme`, override button/input component tokens, and verify both disconnected and connected wallet states for contrast.

## Read Resilient On-Chain Data

- [Detailed guide: Data](blocks/data.md)
- Source: [1001-digital/dapp-query](https://github.com/1001-digital/dapp-query)
- Packages: `@1001-digital/dapp-query-core`, `@1001-digital/dapp-query-vue`
- Use for: queries that should survive indexer downtime, RPC slowness, endpoint failure, duplicate sources, browser reloads, and live chain updates.
- Key rule: define the data shape once, then compose indexed sources and RPC sources behind one query client.

## Fetch And Normalize Dweb Metadata

- [Detailed guide: Metadata](blocks/metadata.md)
- Sources: [dweb-fetch](https://github.com/1001-digital/dweb-fetch), [normalize-dweb-url](https://github.com/1001-digital/normalize-dweb-url), [resolve-metadata](https://github.com/1001-digital/resolve-metadata)
- Packages: `@1001-digital/dweb-fetch`, `@1001-digital/normalize-dweb-url`, `@1001-digital/resolve-metadata`
- Use for: `ipfs://`, `ipns://`, `ar://`, gateway URLs, raw CIDs, `eip155:` NFT references, ERC-721 metadata, ERC-1155 metadata, and `contractURI` metadata.
- Key rule: normalize identifiers before storing them, fetch through dweb-aware clients, then normalize metadata before rendering.

## Index Chain Events

- [Detailed guide: Indexing](blocks/indexing.md)
- Sources: [simple-indexer](https://github.com/1001-digital/simple-indexer), [ponder-artifacts](https://github.com/1001-digital/ponder-artifacts), [ponder-ens](https://github.com/1001-digital/ponder-ens)
- Packages: `@1001-digital/simple-indexer`, `@1001-digital/ponder-artifacts`, `@1001-digital/ponder-ens`
- Use for: lightweight event indexing, browser IndexedDB indexes, server SQLite indexes, local replay, Ponder NFT metadata caches, and Ponder ENS profile caches.
- Key rule: choose `simple-indexer` when you own a small local index; choose the Ponder helpers when you are already inside a Ponder app.

## Build NFT Contracts

- [Detailed guide: Contracts](blocks/contracts.md)
- Sources: [erc721-extensions](https://github.com/1001-digital/erc721-extensions), [check-address](https://github.com/1001-digital/check-address)
- Packages: `@1001-digital/erc721-extensions`, `@1001-digital/check-address`
- Use for: OpenZeppelin-based ERC-721/ERC-1155 extensions, supply assignment, minting helpers, metadata helpers, and address-type checks.
- Key rule: use `check-address` only when the constructor-bypass limitation is acceptable for the product/security model.

## Inspect Contracts And Proxies

- [Detailed guide: Contract Intelligence](blocks/contract-intelligence.md)
- Sources: [proxies](https://github.com/1001-digital/proxies), [natspec](https://github.com/1001-digital/natspec)
- Packages: `@1001-digital/proxies`, `@1001-digital/natspec`
- Use for: EIP-1967 proxies, EIP-2535 diamonds, EIP-1167 clones, beacons, Safe proxies, implementation discovery, composite ABI workflows, and verified-contract NatSpec.
- Key rule: use these for contract-aware apps and developer tools; bring your own verifier/source/ABI enrichment when needed.

## Add Wallets And Auth

- [Detailed guide: Wallet Auth](blocks/wallet-auth.md)
- Sources: [wagmi-in-app-wallet](https://github.com/1001-digital/wagmi-in-app-wallet), [adonis-siwe](https://github.com/1001-digital/adonis-siwe)
- Packages: `@1001-digital/wagmi-in-app-wallet`, `@1001-digital/adonis-siwe`
- Use for: local mnemonic-based wagmi wallets, onboarding/test wallets, and Sign-In with Ethereum sessions in AdonisJS backends.
- Key rule: never hide key custody from users; treat in-app wallet storage as local-key material and use SIWE only when a server-trusted wallet session is needed.

## Run IPFS Infrastructure

- [Detailed guide: Infra](blocks/infra.md)
- Source: [1001-digital/ipfs.server](https://github.com/1001-digital/ipfs.server)
- Use for: deployable Kubo IPFS node infrastructure with a public pinned-content gateway and authenticated admin API.
- Key rule: this is infrastructure, not an app dependency. Use it when the project needs its own pinning/gateway/IPNS operations.
